standard_prerequisites.name: The first coupling event
standard_prerequisites.statement: The event E1 controls the total mass of the point process and fails when some level exceeds the logarithm of x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the event whose complement is estimated.

standard_prerequisites.name: Moments of the limiting variable
standard_prerequisites.statement: The exponential moment of the limiting variable is bounded uniformly, hence the probability that it exceeds the iterated logarithm is of the order one over the logarithm.
standard_prerequisites.use: It removes the region where the level exceeds the iterated logarithm.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exponential law of the truncated weighted sum
standard_prerequisites.statement: The truncated weighted sum is exponentially distributed with parameter equal to the level.
standard_prerequisites.use: It bounds the tail probability appearing after the expectation is computed.

core_obligations: Use the moment bound to show that the level exceeds the iterated logarithm only with probability of the order one over the logarithm, and reduce the estimate to a sum over the two possible values of the parity index (source lines 892-894).

Show that a point with large weight and a level close to the logarithm forces the truncated weighted sum to exceed the logarithm minus the iterated logarithm, and bound the probability of that by the exponential tail bound (source lines 897-900).

Compute the expectation of the sum over the points of the process with the Mecke equation, integrate against the exponential density in the weights, and evaluate the resulting one-dimensional integral to obtain the stated order (source lines 900-961).

proof_roadmap.step: Remove the region of large level by the moment bound and split into the two parity cases.
Reduce the remaining event to a tail event for the truncated weighted sum.
Evaluate the expectation with the Mecke equation and integrate.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 886-889: the first coupling event fails with probability of the order one over the logarithm of x. The proof (source lines 891-961) combines four mechanisms that the statement does not mention: the exponential moment bound removes the region in which the level exceeds the iterated logarithm; the failure of the event is then rewritten as a sum over the two parities of the level being close to the logarithm while the corresponding weight is not too small; that condition is in turn shown to force the truncated weighted sum beyond a threshold, where the exponential tail bound applies; and the remaining expectation of a sum over the points of the process is computed with the Mecke equation before the resulting integral is evaluated. The author notes that the argument needs more care than the corresponding step of the paper it refines.
